  opens the file through the source with its own actor, so access and classification are checked
  again; a changed file has another hash, and a reader the turn would no longer choose, or may no
  longer send the file to, gets nothing from it. A kept text is read instead of calling the reader.
- `FileRead` and `FileRefused` business events carry `FileId`, `FileName`, `FileMediaType`,
  `FileHash`, how the file reached the turn as `ObjectId` (`NhAssistantFileOrigins`) and, for a
  tool result, the tool and invocation. `FileName` is the reference's name, at most 256 characters,
  without control, format or separator characters and in Unicode normalization form C: the only free
  text of the event. `FileReaderId` names the reading tool that read, refused or failed the file:
  the reader id, or `mcp.<server>` with `McpConnectionOwner` for an MCP server; for a file a reader
  read, `FileHash` is the SHA-256 of the content the reader received and `FileTextCached` says whether
  the text was the conversation's kept text. File content and a reader's text never reach logs,
  audit or usage records, and the file's name stays out of logs.

A reading tool of the application, registered next to the file source. NewHeap's packages carry no
document library; the sample's `OfficeDocumentReader` (SPM-305) is an example to copy, which reads
Word and Excel documents with DocumentFormat.OpenXml in the application's own process:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .AddFileReader<OfficeDocumentReader>("office-documents", reader => reader
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Docx, NhAiMediaTypes.Xlsx)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal, NhAiDataClassification.Confidential)));
```

- Bound what a reader unpacks, such as OpenXml's `OpenSettings.MaxCharactersInPart`, and return a
  failed result for a damaged document instead of text cut off; the turn's limits count the text.
- A part bound is no bound on the text: cells can name one shared string again and again, and
  several sheets can name one worksheet, so the text can be far longer than the file. Bound the
  text while it is made, value by value, by `NhAssistantFileReadRequest.MaxTextCharacters`, the
  characters the turn can still take, and stop with a failed result with
  `NhAssistantErrorCodes.FileTokenLimit`, which refuses the file with `assistant-file-token-limit`;
  read each part once and check the `cancellationToken` at every row or paragraph. MCP readers get
  the same budget host-side: a longer text is refused before its blocks are joined.

People attach files to a chat message in two steps. First the client uploads each file to the
conversation with `POST {prefix}/conversations/{id}/files`: `multipart/form-data` with one file part
named `file` and the header `X-NH-Assistant-Upload: 1`, which a cross-site form cannot send, so the
endpoint keeps the posture of the JSON endpoints under the same access policy. The endpoint checks, in
this order, the conversation and the agent's policy (as for a message), a file source
(`assistant-files-unavailable`), an agent that accepts files (`assistant-files-not-accepted`), one
named, non-empty file part (`assistant-file-upload-invalid`), an accepted media type whose content
starts as files of that type do (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`), the agent's `MaxFileBytes`
(`assistant-file-too-large`) and, when the application registered one, its upload scanner
(`INhAssistantUploadScanner` with `ConfigureUploads(uploads => uploads.UseScanner<T>())`): a file it
refuses answers `assistant-file-scan-refused` (422), a scan that could not run
(`assistant-file-upload-failed` from the scanner, or an exception) answers
`assistant-file-upload-failed` (503), and nothing is stored; without a scanner nothing is scanned.
Only then does `StoreUploadAsync` receive the file, with the name
without its path, the media type lowercase and `NhAssistantFileUpload.Classification`; it answers the
`NhAiFileReference` the endpoint returns. A refusal of the source answers
`assistant-file-upload-refused` (422) unless it is `assistant-file-too-large`,
`assistant-file-type-not-accepted` or `assistant-files-unavailable`; an exception or an invalid
reference answers `assistant-file-upload-failed` (503) and logs only its type. Then the message carries
the references in `files` of `POST conversations/{id}/messages` (`NhAssistantSendMessageRequest.Files`),
at most the agent's files per turn, and the turn opens them as described above.

Browsers send no media type, or a generic one, for files their system does not know, and Windows
names some extensions after the program that opens them, such as `application/vnd.ms-excel` for a
`.csv` file. A file part without a type, with `application/octet-stream` (or
`binary/octet-stream`, `application/unknown`) or with such a type for its extension therefore takes
the type its file name's extension names, but only a type the application accepts; the content check
and the scanner then run as for any upload. A specific type the application does not accept stays
refused (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`): the extension never overrides it, and an extension of a
type the application does not accept names nothing. `text/xml` counts as such a type for `.xml`, whose
type is `application/xml`; an application that accepts `text/xml` but not `application/xml` keeps
receiving `text/xml`. Accept `text/csv` to take CSV exports; when the application also accepts
`application/vnd.ms-excel`, a `.csv` sent with that type still becomes `text/csv`. The
composer of `@newheap/platform-ai-chat` applies the same table before it uploads and declares the
type it derived.

The platform's table knows `.pdf`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`,
`.pptx`, `.doc`, `.xls`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.json` and `.xml`. Map the
application's own extensions with `NhAssistantUploadOptions.MapExtension(extension, mediaType)`, such
as `.dwg` to `application/acad`: the derivation then uses the mapping exactly like the table, only while
the application accepts the mapped type, and a mapping of an extension the table knows takes
precedence over the table. `MapExtension` throws for an extension that is not a dot with letters,
digits, `_`, `+` or `-` (at most 32 characters), a value that is not a media type, or more than
`MaxMappedExtensions` (100) extensions. The agents' upload rules carry the mappings of accepted types
(`NhAssistantAgentUploadsDto.MappedExtensions`), so the composer derives alike and its file picker
offers the extensions. The sample maps `.jfif` to JPEG (SPM-305).

The content check also covers text: an upload whose type resolves to `text/*`, `application/json`,
`application/xml` or a `+json` or `+xml` type is refused (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`) when its
content starts with the signature of an OLE2 compound file (Word, Excel or PowerPoint 97 to 2003), a
ZIP package, a PDF, or a PNG, JPEG or GIF image, such as an `.xls` workbook renamed to `.csv`. There is
no NUL-byte check, so UTF-16 text, such as Excel's "Unicode text" export, passes. A `.pptx` must start as
a ZIP package, as a `.docx` and an `.xlsx` must. Check the rest of the content of the text types the
application accepts in its scanner or file source.

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .ConfigureUploads(uploads =>
    {
        // PDF, PNG, JPEG, Word and Excel by default; no types switches uploads off.
        uploads.AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg);
        // An extension the platform's table does not know names an accepted type.
        uploads.MapExtension(".jfif", NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg);
        // Confidential by default: the profile, or a fallback, must permit it.
        uploads.DefaultClassification = NhAiDataClassification.Confidential;
        // Every upload passes the application's scanner before the file source stores it.
        uploads.UseScanner<EicarUploadScanner>();
    }));
```

- A scanner (scoped) receives the checked upload and its actor and returns `TaskResult`: a failed
  result refuses the file, a failed result with `assistant-file-upload-failed` says the scan could not
  run. Its messages are never shown or logged. The sample's `EicarUploadScanner` (SPM-305) refuses
  the EICAR test string; a real application calls its virus scanner there.

- Store the classification of an upload with the file and report it from `OpenAsync`; raise it when
  the application knows the content is more sensitive. Uploads that no message ends up carrying stay
  in the application's storage under its own retention.
- Let uploads go with their conversation with `UseFileRetention<T>()`, where `T` implements
  `INhAssistantFileRetention`. The assistant calls `ForgetConversationAsync` with a
  `NhAssistantForgottenConversation` (the conversation, its agent and tenant, the subject of a thread
  and the reason, `archived` or `subject-forgotten` of `NhAssistantFileRetentionReasons`) after the
  owner's archive of a chat committed (`DELETE conversations/{id}`; a participant who leaves forgets
  nothing) and after `INhAiSubjectRetention.ForgetSubjectAsync` deleted each agent's thread. It is best
  effort: a failed result or an exception is logged as a warning with the conversation and the code or
  exception type, never undoes the archive or the deletion and is not retried. Make it idempotent, so
  that forgetting a conversation without uploads or one forgotten before succeeds and the
  application's own retention can call it again for one it missed. The sample's
  `ProjectMediaUploadRetention` (SPM-359) removes the conversation's upload folder from the media
  library.
- The endpoint lowers the request body limit of an upload to the agent's `MaxFileBytes` plus 16 KB,
  but never raises the server's own limit (Kestrel's `MaxRequestBodySize`, 30 MB by default); raise
  that one too when `MaxFileBytes` is larger.
- `GET status` and `GET agents` give each agent `uploads` (`NhAssistantAgentUploadsDto`) with the
  accepted media types, the largest file and the most files of one message, or `null` when people can
  attach nothing to it, so a client checks a file before it uploads it. An agent offers uploads only
  when its profile or a fallback permits, in the execution region, the classification a message with
  an upload carries: the higher of the agent's own and `DefaultClassification`. Otherwise `uploads` is
  `null` and an upload answers `409 assistant-files-not-accepted`, instead of an offered upload that
  the turn then refuses with `assistant-classification-not-permitted`. The sample's quick answers agent
  runs on a profile for internal data only and offers none (SPM-359).
- The conversation shows a person's attachments as `file` parts (`NhAssistantFilePartDto`) with name,
  media type and size, also in the live `message.created` event; never the content, the application's
  id or a hash. Files a tool returned stay named in that call's result, which follows the viewer's
  rights to it. A message with attachments in a busy agent thread waits for the next run with its
  files (`202` with the trigger receipt), unless the agent takes no files
  (`assistant-files-not-accepted`) or fewer (`assistant-file-count-limit`); the run opens them as
  attachments with the rights of the person who wrote the message, within the limits of the skill it
  works in, and a file it cannot open is named to the model with its code instead.

## Agent threads

An agent that runs on its own (see the agent-runs rule) keeps one thread per agent and
subject in the same `nhai` schema. A thread is a conversation of kind `thread`; it never
appears in a person's conversation list, and nobody owns it: the subject's access
resolver decides on every request who reads it, who types in it and who decides its
proposals. A person who types in a thread starts a turn in which that person is the
initiator; such a turn is bound to the request like a chat turn, its approvals are
always inline, and a message that arrives while a run is active waits for the next
run (`202 Accepted` with a receipt). Request-bound turns end with the request, and
their cancellation reaches only the process that runs them; work that must outlive a
request belongs in an agent run.

## Context for a reviewed MCP tool

When a remote service needs the conversation to answer, keep its model-facing schema
small (for example only `question`) and send the context as request metadata instead.
Register the reviewed tool in code with `AddMcpContextBinding(new
NhAssistantMcpContextBinding(serverId, serverUrl, remoteName))`. The binding applies
only while an administrator connects the server under that id and URL; any other
server, URL or tool never receives the context. Each call then carries `_meta` key
`com.newheap/assistant-context` with the acting agent, the accountable person, the
conversation, turn and tool invocation ids, the approval and proposal ids of an approved
call and, unless `IncludeSnapshot` is off, a bounded snapshot: the first question plus
the latest completed user and assistant text within `NhAssistantConversationSnapshotRequest`
(`MaxRecentMessages`, `MaxBytes`, `MaxMessageBytes`), with omitted messages and bytes.
Code that needs the snapshot elsewhere inside a tool call uses
`INhAssistantConversationSnapshotProvider` with the call's invocation context. It
verifies the running call, the run, the accountable actor's access and the active turn
itself, and never returns instructions, tool calls or results, approvals, page context
or output of the running turn, also not text written before an approval pause.

## Consultation chains across applications

When cooperating applications consult each other's agents over MCP, let them keep one
consultation chain, so a loop between them is refused as one host refuses it (SPM-366). Name
the application once with `UseMcpChainApplication(applicationId)`, for example its public origin
or token issuer: 1 to `NhAssistantMcpContext.MaxApplicationIdLength` characters without white
space or control characters (`IsApplicationId`). Every application of a chain needs a name of
its own.

On the sending side set `IncludeChain = true` on the `NhAssistantMcpContextBinding` of the other
application's consult tool. The assistant context then also carries `chain`: `agents`, the agents
that asked, outermost first and each as `{ "application", "agentId" }`, ending with the calling
turn's own agent, and `consultationDepth`, the depth of the calling turn (0 outside a
consultation). The version stays 1 and the other members keep their shape, so a receiver that does
not know `chain` reads the rest as before. A consultation turn offers no administrator-connected MCP
tools, so a consulted agent reaches another application through a code-owned import
(`INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`) whose policy names `InvocationBinderId =
NhAssistantMcpContext.BinderId` for the binding's server id and remote name. With the chain the
binding also binds a call from a consultation turn: its `conversation` names the consulted agent's
thread and the consultation as turn, and it carries no snapshot.

On the receiving side register every reviewed caller with `ContinueMcpChain(new
NhAssistantMcpChainCaller(applicationId, issuer))`. A request is from that caller when its
authenticated principal carries exactly one `IssuerClaimType` claim (`iss`) with the issuer and,
for an issuer that serves several applications, exactly one `ClientClaimType` claim with
`ClientId`. A consultation such a caller starts over MCP begins where its chain ended: one level
deeper than the deeper of the caller's depth and this application's own, with the caller's agents
counted as askers, each qualified by its application. `MaxConsultationDepth` then bounds the whole
path, and an agent of this application already in the chain, also on a path that never returns to
the application that asked first, refuses the call with `assistant-consult-depth-exceeded` before a
consultation is recorded or the agent runs. Two applications with an agent of the same id never
refuse each other. A request (`assistant.request.*`) whose chain comes from a consultation is
refused the same way, as one host never offers a request inside a consultation. The chain of any
other caller is ignored, never refused, so an ordinary MCP client keeps working: the call is a
direct call at depth 1. A malformed chain of a reviewed caller is ignored too, with a warning that
names the problem and not the payload: another version, a missing or non-integer depth, no agents
or more than `MaxChainAgents`, an invalid application or agent id, or a calling agent of another
application than the caller's. The consultation keeps `AskingAgentId` `null`, because no agent of
this application asked, and counts the chain in `Depth`.

The chain is loop protection between cooperating applications, not authorization. The caller's
person still needs the consultation's policy and a role on the subject, and the consulted agent's
daily `Budget`, `MaxConsultationsPerActorPerDay` and the call's deadline bound a caller that sends
no chain or a forged one: a forged shallow chain costs budget, never correctness.

## Compositions and scripts: a switch the application owns

A composition runs a known chain of governed tools as one tool, and the script tool runs a short
program the model writes over the tools of its turn. Both mark their descriptor with
`NhAiToolDescriptor.CompositionFeature` (`NhAiCompositionFeature.Compositions` or `Scripts`); every
other tool keeps `None` and nothing below ever affects it. A marked tool is offered only where three
things allow it, decided once per feature at the start of each turn, run step and MCP request:

1. **Code** sets the ceiling. An agent in code opts in with
   `ConfigureAgentContext(agentId, c => c.AllowCompositions().AllowScripts())`. Agents created in the
   administration get them only within `UseCompositionsAsData(c => c.AllowCompositions().AllowScripts())`,
   and then each such agent carries its own `compositions` and `scripts` setting, saved and versioned
   with its definition, carried in agent packages only when on and taken over by a promoted shadow
   variant; switching on what the ceiling does not allow answers `compositions: not-allowed` or
   `scripts: not-allowed` (`NhAssistantFieldErrors.NotAllowed`), while a setting the agent already has
   stays accepted. An MCP exposure opts in with `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools(mcp => mcp.AllowCompositions().AllowScripts())`.
2. **The application's switch** decides at run time: `INhAssistantCompositionSwitch.IsOnAsync` with
   `NhAssistantCompositionSwitchContext` (the feature, the channel `Chat`, `Run`, `Consultation`,
   `HandOff` or `Mcp`, the tenant, the agent, `null` for MCP, and the person: the person who chats,
   a run's initiator, the person who asked a consultation, the MCP caller). The default reads
   `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Compositions` and `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Scripts`, both off. An application
   that offers the features as a setting of its own registers `UseCompositionSwitch<TSwitch>()`, a
   scoped service that reads its own table with a cache of its own, because it is asked every turn.
   The switch is asked only where code allows the feature and a tool of it is registered; one that
   throws counts as off and only the exception type is logged.
3. **The tool** must be registered in a catalog (`Agent` exposure for agents, `Mcp` for the export).
   Compositions are selected by the agent's tool selectors like any tool; the script tool needs no
   selector, also not in a consultation's own selection, because the ceiling is its opt-in and a script
   only calls the tools its turn offers. Effect and autonomy rules still apply to both.

A value that changes during a turn applies from the next one, so a running script never flips halfway.
While a feature is off its tools are not offered to the model and not listed over MCP, and a call that
still arrives, such as an approved proposal of a composition or an MCP call from an earlier list, is
refused with `assistant-composition-off` or `assistant-scripting-off` before anything runs; a marked
tool the MCP exposure does not allow is not part of it (`ai-tool-not-authorized`).

`INhAssistantCompositionStatus.GetAsync` and `GET admin/agents/{id}/compositions` (administration
policy) return what the assistant actually does for one agent, per feature and per channel, and why
(`NhAssistantCompositionReasons`): `on`, `not-installed` (no tool of the feature; for scripts the
scripting package), `agent-not-allowed` (an agent in code), `not-allowed-for-data-agents` or
`off-for-agent` (an agent created in the administration) and `off-by-application`. The switch is asked
for the reading person and tenant. Show it next to the application's own checkbox, as the
administration's agent page does. The run catalog reports `compositionCeiling`. The sample stores its
setting per environment and agent in its own table and switches the project assistant and the scripting
desk, an agent created as data (SPM-371).

## Compositions and the step runtime

Declare a known chain of governed tools as one tool with `AddComposition<TInput>(id, ...)` when the
model would otherwise read every intermediate result to choose the next call (SPM-372). The steps
call registered tools by id, in order; a later step takes values from earlier results through
`NhAssistantCompositionContext<TInput>.Result`, and `Returns` declares the only data that reaches the
model. Prefer a composition over a hand-written `[NhAiTool]` that calls services directly: that tool
loses per-step rights, approval, guards, budget and audit.

```csharp
assistant.AddComposition<ProjectOverviewInput>("projects.overview", composition => composition
    .Describe("Show one project with its open tasks and its members in one call.")
    .ExposeOverMcp()
    .Step("project", "projects.get", context => new { projectId = context.Input.ProjectId })
    .Step("open-tasks", "projects.list-open-tasks", context => new
    {
        projectId = context.Result("project").GetProperty("id").GetGuid()
    })
    .Returns(context => new { project = context.Result("project"), openTasks = context.Result("open-tasks") }));
```

- The composition is a tool marked `NhAiCompositionFeature.Compositions`. Its effect is the strongest
  effect of its steps and its classification the highest, so one that only reads runs at once and is
  read-only over MCP. An agent's tool selectors select it where code allows compositions
  (`ConfigureAgentContext(...).AllowCompositions()`) and the application's switch has them on, and a
  turn offers it only together with every tool its steps call. With `ExposeOverMcp` an exposure that
  allows compositions lists it; its steps must be exposed there too.
- Every step runs through the shared invoker with the caller's context and gets exactly the decision
  the same call gets on its own. A `Deferred` proposal returns the usual "proposal recorded" result and
  the chain continues; a later step that reads its result stops the chain with
  `assistant-composition-step-result-unavailable`. An `Inline` approval stops the chain, the turn
  waits as it does for a call of the model, and after the decision the model reads its own call, where
  the chain stopped, and the decided step. A shadow run proposes every change and executes none. A step
  that fails or is refused stops the chain; the model receives what succeeded and that step's code.
- Steps never call another composition, the script tool, a consultation or a destructive tool, and a
  step's files are not opened: return what the model needs through `Returns`.
- Over MCP, and for any caller outside a turn, a step runs through its governed function: a step that
  needs approval fails with `ai-tool-approval-required`, as the same call does there.

The step runtime is public for the script tool and for an application's own chain tool: from inside
the tool's governed function call `INhAssistantToolSteps.BeginAsync` with an
`NhAssistantToolStepRequest` (`MaxSteps`, `MaxMutationSteps`, `Hash`, `Tools`), run each step with
`NhAssistantToolStepSession.RunAsync`, stop when a step's `NhAssistantToolStepStatus` says so or the
session is `Stopped`, and call `CompleteAsync` once with the result the model receives. In a turn a step
may call only a tool the agent is offered in that turn; outside a turn only a tool the caller may
discover through the same exposure. Each step is a tool invocation of the turn whose call id names the
call that ran it; the message shows one card for the call, the first step uses its count of the turn's
tool calls and every further step counts as a call of its own. Every step's context, audit record and
proposal guard context carry `NhAiToolCallOrigin` (see the protected-actions rule).

The agent's Activity in the administration shows each composition and script call with the tool calls
it ran in order, the model rounds it saved (its tool calls minus one) and the size of the result
returned to the model, and per tool what the calls saved: `GET admin/agents/{id}/compositions/activity`
(`NhAssistantCompositionActivityDto`), `getAgentCompositionActivity` and the Compositions view of
`nh-assistant-agent-composition-activity`. It reads the stored tool invocations and is content-free;
calls in a consultation store nothing and are not listed.

## Avoid

- Calling `AddNewHeapAssistant` before `AddNewHeapPlatformAIAspNet` or replacing the
  invocation gate, budget, idempotency or evidence manager afterwards; startup fails.
- Believing a consultation chain from a caller you did not review with `ContinueMcpChain`, or
  reading the chain as authorization; it only ever refuses, and budgets and limits still bound a
  forged one.
- Giving two applications of a chain the same name, or reviewing a caller under this application's
  own name: agents of the same id would refuse each other, and startup refuses the second. A binding
  with `IncludeChain` or a reviewed caller without `UseMcpChainApplication` fails startup too.
- Registering or replacing `INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy` for the assistant; discovery
  stays owned by the application or the API bridge.
- Offering a composition or the script tool as an extra function outside a tool catalog, or reading
  the application's setting yourself in a tool: only marked catalog tools follow the switch, the
  ceiling and the refusal codes. Do not read a database without a cache in
  `INhAssistantCompositionSwitch`; it is asked every turn.
- Adding agent-specific copies of tools to bypass approval, or approving on behalf
  of the user from code.
- Letting an impersonation session record a personal grant of the impersonated person, such as
  background-use consent, a personal MCP connection or a push subscription, in an endpoint of your
  own; refuse it as the assistant does with `assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating` and keep
  withdrawals open.
- Issuing a channel credential, such as a messaging link token, from an impersonation session, binding
  it to nothing but the person's id, or renewing it with a full lifetime from itself; it would act as
  the person after the impersonation, the password change or the revocation that should end it.
- Writing prompts, messages, tool arguments or results to logs, `INhAiAuditSink`,
  usage records or `INhAssistantBusinessAuditSink`; those receive identifiers,
  versions, codes and timestamps only.
- Applying the library migrations to a shared database without an explicit
  deployment decision; `RunMigrations` is off by default.
- Relying on `POST cancel` across nodes; it reaches turns in the same process, and
  an abandoned running turn is recovered after its deadline.
- Starting a person's turn from a channel by calling the application's own assistant endpoints with
  a service credential, or by authorizing tools against the channel's request; use
  `INhAssistantConversationTurns`, whose tools authorize the person it names. Never pass a principal
  the application did not authenticate as that person.
- Expecting `KeepTurnsAfterDisconnect` to resume a stream; the client reloads the conversation.
- Reading the turn's person from `IHttpContextAccessor` in a tool, policy or turn context provider; a
  channel's turn and a turn that outlived its request have no request of the person. Inject
  `INhAiTurnPerson`.
- Calling the endpoints to create, list, read, stop or answer a person's chat, list their agents or
  upload a file from a channel; use `INhAssistantConversations` and
  `INhAssistantConversationTurns.AnswerAsync`. Implementing or mocking `INhAssistantConversations`
  outside the application's own tests: it grows with the endpoints.
- Passing a forward-only stream to `UploadAsync`, or logging the name of an upload in a scanner, file
  source or file retention.
- Trusting remote MCP annotations such as `readOnlyHint`; they are hints for the
  administrator only. Mark a remote tool read-only only after reviewing it.
- Forwarding user tokens to hosts outside `ForwardUserTokenHosts`, or allowing plain
  http, link-local or metadata addresses for MCP servers.
- Writing MCP server, tool or assignment rows from application code, or calling the administration's
  endpoints from the application's own backend; use `INhAssistantMcpServers`, which keeps the checks,
  secrets and audit. Turning `AllowLoopback` on outside test hosts.
- Setting `headlessUse` to `organization` for a server whose credential lets an agent
  do more than the people it works for may; background runs then act with it.
- Sharing the HS256 signing key with a first-party MCP server so that it can validate delegated
  tokens; sign asymmetrically and let it validate with the published keys. Letting the assistant's
  own host `Accept` delegated MCP tokens on more than its MCP endpoint.
- Writing a secret resolver that maps a reference name to arbitrary settings, files or
  environment variables; a name selects one secret of one source.
- Forwarding a person's own NewHeap token from an application's credential provider; exchange it
  for a token of the MCP server instead, and keep the provider's client secret in the secrets file.
- Using an organization connection for a system that must know who acts, such as a mailbox or a
  calendar; let each person connect (`connectionScope: user`).
- Connecting an organization `oauth` server with a personal or administrator account;
  everyone using the server's agents acts as it. Connect a service account and name it in
  `organizationAccountLabel`.
- Confirming an authorization server that the administration did not expect, or adding
  the host's own pages to `ReturnOrigins` from configuration that users control.
- Putting permissions, approval rules or scope decisions in the application context or
  the preferences; they explain the domain and shape style only.
- Listing the application's entities in the application context; use the application map.
- Deciding access from page context or provider facts. Entity ids on the user's screen are
  search hints; authorization and division scope stay with the tools and the gate.
- Putting secrets, tokens or model input into provider facts.
- Sharing a conversation that holds confidential tool results with people who may not
  see them: participants read the whole history, including result previews.
- Returning people of another tenant from `INhAssistantParticipantDirectory`, or
  trusting an actor id from the client without resolving it in the directory.
- Letting a participant decide another participant's approval, or treating the
  conversation owner as the actor of every turn.
- Committing VAPID private keys, widening `AllowedEndpointHosts` to arbitrary hosts or
  putting message content into notification texts.
- Sending a conversation's updates or notifications to its stored participant rows without
  its read rule, or keeping a hub connection, push subscription or participant row of a person
  whose session ended or whose account the platform deleted.
- Binding the assistant context to a server id without its reviewed URL, asking the model
  to repeat conversation text as tool arguments, or treating the metadata as
  authorization on the remote side.
- Returning file content, base64 or extracted text in a tool's data to show the model a document;
  return references and let the file source open them with the turn's actor.
- Checking access to a file only in the tool that names it; `OpenAsync` decides for every turn,
  also a later one with another actor.
- Declaring media types in `AcceptMediaTypes` that the model behind the profile cannot read, or
  reporting a file as less sensitive than it is.
- Setting an MCP server up as reader with a `maxClassification` above what may leave the platform
  for that server, or letting a reader of the application send files to an external service
  without limiting its classifications with `PermitDataClassifications`.
- Showing a reader's own error messages or logging its text: a document can carry anything.
- Storing an upload without `NhAssistantFileUpload.Classification`, or trusting the declared media
  type of an application-specific upload type without checking its content in `StoreUploadAsync`.
- Writing into conversations through the store or a person's message endpoint to report what the
  application did; post an application message with `INhAssistantConversationMessages`.
- Choosing `WithoutPersonCheck()` for a conversation a client named instead of `ReadableBy`, posting
  from retried background work without an `IdempotencyKey`, or writing instructions for the model
  into an application message that is not `Trusted`.
- Putting user-generated data into a `Trusted` application message, escaped or not, or putting
  people's data into an application message's Markdown without `NhAssistantMarkdown.Escape`.

## Verification

With an impersonation principal (the person's claims plus `ImpersonateOriginUserId`), assert on
SQL Server and PostgreSQL that consent, starting and completing a personal OAuth connection and a
push subscription answer `403 assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating` and store nothing, that a
completion refused this way ends the flow, and that withdrawing consent, disconnecting and removing
a subscription succeed with the impersonating user in `ImpersonationOriginActorId`.

Drive turns with `NhAiScriptedChatClient` against real SQL Server and PostgreSQL:
a read-only turn with one tool call, a mutation that pauses for approval and
resumes after approve, a reject that closes without executing, an expired
proposal, an exhausted daily budget, the tool-call limit, cancel and a disabled
flag. For `AllowQuestions`, assert that a question waits, that its addressee's answer resumes the
turn with the answer as the call's result, that another participant is refused, that a question
expires on the application's clock and that a stopped turn cancels it, and that an agent without the
opt-in offers no `ask_question`. Script a provider error inside the stream with
`RespondWithProviderError("server_is_overloaded")` and assert that one retry answers, that
a repeated or non-transient error fails the turn with `assistant-model-unavailable`, and
that the failed conversation accepts the next message. At the tool-call limit, assert a closing answer from a request with tool choice
`none` that carries every call's result, no further tool execution, and a follow-up
turn whose history holds the tool-call summary but no result content. Send one call with flat arguments and one with `input` mixed with another
property, and assert the first succeeds and the second returns `ai-tool-input-invalid`
before a corrected retry succeeds. Assert that no prompt, argument, result or answer text reaches the audit,
usage and business sinks or logs, that approval is bound to the proposal hash and
owner, and that the SSE event and JSON property names match the contract.
Unit-test each tool presenter without a host: present with the longest texts the application
stores, in every supported culture with that culture current, and assert that
`NhAssistantPresentationLimits.FindBrokenRule` returns `null` (SPM-347).
With `KeepTurnsAfterDisconnect`, disconnect a client while the model waits and assert that the turn
completes and is stored, that its tool call after the disconnect authorizes the captured principal,
that the turn is cancelled without the option and that `POST cancel` still stops it. Through
`INhAssistantConversationTurns`, assert on both providers a sent message and a decided approval with
the channel in the audit, refusals of a person outside the conversation, without the access or the
agent's policy, of another actor or tenant than the principal, and a tool policy decided by the
person and not by the request around the call (SPM-332). Through `INhAssistantConversations` and
`AnswerAsync`, assert on both providers a chat created, read and stopped, an answered question with
the channel in the audit, the answer's refusals in their order and its expiry on a test clock, and the
refusals of another person, another tenant and an agent thread. Assert that a test turn context
provider, a tool policy and a tool see `ConversationId`, `Channel` and `INhAiTurnPerson` in a turn of
the endpoints and in a channel's turn (SPM-341, SPM-342). Assert on both providers that
`ListAsync`, `ListAgentsAsync` and `UploadAsync` give the endpoints' lists and refusals (size, type,
content, name, agent, profile chain, scanner, file source, someone outside the chat, a participant
without the agent's policy, the access policy, another person's principal), that the stream is read
again from the caller's position and stays the caller's, and that no log names the file (SPM-358).
Assert that an archive and subject retention call `ForgetConversationAsync` once per conversation, a
participant who leaves none, and that a failing or throwing retention only warns while the
conversation stays gone; and that `GET agents` offers uploads only where the profile chain permits the
uploads' classification (SPM-359). With a test clock, assert that a message
closes a question and an approval that passed their lifetime with the late answer's or decision's
codes and audit and then starts its turn, and that a still valid one keeps the chat busy. With Web
Push, assert that a question notifies its addressee only, and an approval the person whose turn it is.
For administration, assert version conflicts, the admin policy, the seed behavior and
the composed instruction order with an injection attempt in the custom instructions.
For situational and page context, assert the block order and markers, the limits, that
an invalid `clientContext` is ignored, that a failing provider does not stop the turn,
that the prompt hash and a pending approval survive another page, and that facts and
page text never reach audit or logs (SPM-254).
For MCP, use an official SDK server (in memory or Streamable HTTP): tools are off after
sync and visible only to the assigned agent after activation, mutations pause for
approval, schema changes disable tools, blocked hosts are rejected and secrets are
absent from responses, logs and audit. Through `INhAssistantMcpServers`, assert on both providers that
a created server never returns its secret, an update with a `null` secret keeps it, sync and tool
updates audit as the administration does, an assignment offers the tools to the agent without a new
agent version and is audited once, the per-agent limit refuses another server and the host guard
refuses what the administration refuses. Assert that an agent save without `mcpServerIds` keeps an
assignment made after the editor read the agent, that `[]` clears them, and that the assignment
endpoints answer `403` without the admin policy and the service's codes and audit with it (SPM-345).
For a consultation chain across applications, run real hosts with their own MCP endpoints and
code-owned imports of each other's consult tools, and assert: A consults B and B consulting A back
is refused with `assistant-consult-depth-exceeded` before a consultation is recorded or a model
runs; A asks B, B asks C and C asks B is refused at B while A receives no call; the same call from a
caller that was not reviewed is a direct call at depth 1; two applications with an agent of the
same id answer each other; a reviewed caller that sends a shallow chain on every call is refused by
`MaxConsultationsPerActorPerDay`; and a malformed chain of a reviewed caller is ignored, not
refused. Pin the JSON names of `chain` and the shape of the context without it (SPM-366).
For a tool that no sync has seen, assert that it is stored `missing` without a schema and never
offered, that a sync that cannot reach the server or does not see it leaves it waiting, that the first
sync that sees it keeps its settings and a later schema change disables it, and that refused names and
the limit audit nothing (SPM-346). For loopback, assert that a `Testing` host reaches an MCP
server on loopback with `AllowLoopback` and refuses it without, that link-local and metadata hosts stay
blocked, and that a Production host with the option does not start (SPM-331). For background runs, assert on both providers
that a `never` server is not contacted, an `organization` server is offered and
called through a code grant or a person's rights, `requiredPolicy` is evaluated for
that person, an approved deferred MCP proposal executes once, and a server set back to
`never` fails it with `assistant-mcp-headless-not-allowed` without a call. For OAuth, run `NhAiTestAuthorizationServer` with an `NhAiTestProtectedResource` in
front of the MCP server and assert on both providers that nothing is pinned without
confirmation, client credentials request one token for the resource, `insufficient_scope`
steps up within the allowed scopes, an authorization completes only for its starter with
the admin policy after the `state`, `iss` and expiry checks, concurrent renewals send one
refresh request, a refused refresh requires reauthorization, another issuer suspends the
connection and disconnecting revokes the tokens (SPM-299). For personal connections, assert that
a person without one gets the `connection.required` event and part and no tools, that each
person's turn and each colleague in a shared conversation uses their own account, that step-up asks
to connect again, that a run uses the connection only with consent and that an approved proposal
fails as not connected after the person disconnected (SPM-300). For a
`personal` server, assert on both providers that it is skipped without consent, that
every request then carries a fresh delegated token of the person with the invocation
marker and the server's origin, that a withdrawn consent or a changed URL stops it, and
that a refused, unbound or failing issuer sends nothing. For secret references, rotate
the configured or resolved value between two connections and assert that names with
`:` or `..` are refused. SPM-245, SPM-246, SPM-247, SPM-250, SPM-251 and
SPM-252 and SPM-254 are the executable references. SPM-249 is the end-to-end reference: one agent
over the API bridge and curated tools, an administrator agent with an MCP tool, and a
viewer who is offered no mutating tools.
For sharing, assert on both providers that a participant of another tenant never
reaches the conversation, read positions only move forward, concurrent joins of one
person add one row without an EF Core error log and concurrent joins of different people
stay within the participant limit; over HTTP that a wrong or revoked token fails,
the model sees named user messages, the owner cannot decide a participant's approval,
another participant cannot cancel, removal stops access and live updates, and the hub
rejects anonymous connections (SPM-263). Over the real hub, assert on both providers that a
thread's events reach only people whose role holds, also with a stale participant row, a chat's
only participants who pass the agent's policy and only on connections of the chat's tenant, and
that a connection closes when its token expires and when the session validator refuses it
(`AssistantLiveReadRuleTests`, `AssistantHubSessionTests`). For push, check the RFC 8291 test vector,
a verifiable VAPID token, the endpoint allow-list, the notification rules, an
encrypted delivery without message content, the opt-out and the removal of a gone
subscription (SPM-264), and on both providers that Web Push and in-app notifications skip a
participant whose role ended, who fails the agent's policy or whom the platform no longer
resolves, and that forgetting a user removes their subscriptions, notification choice, notices
and participant rows (`AssistantNotificationReadRuleTests`, `AssistantUnresolvedPeopleTests`). For the MCP context, read `_meta` in the server's call handler
over the official transport: the reviewed tool receives the identities and snapshot, the
same tool under another server id or URL receives nothing, an approved call carries its
approval, and the snapshot refuses another person, another invocation or run, a stale
turn and calls outside a tool call while leaving out output of the running turn and
reporting cut text as omitted bytes (SPM-266).

For the application map, assert that an agent with `UseApplicationMap` reads the entries of the tools its turn offers between the instructions and the situation, in order and within the bound, that a changed map changes its hash but not the prompt, that agents without it and a failing source leave the turn without it, and that the sample's assistant queries the tasks of a project with one gateway call (SPM-289).

For files, script a tool that returns a reference and assert on both providers that the next model
request carries the file after the tool results as file content behind the external-data marker,
that the result names `attached` and the hash, that each limit, an undeclared type, a forbidden or
missing file and a file no profile may receive are refused with their own codes, that a
confidential file moves the model calls to the fallback that permits it, that messages, tool calls,
audit and logs hold references and hashes only, and that a later turn opens the file again with its
own actor and names it when that actor may no longer read it. Over HTTP, upload a file and send it with
a message on both providers and assert the stored classification, the file part of the conversation
without content, id or hash, and the codes of a file too large, a type not accepted, content of
another type, an agent that accepts no files and a caller without access. SPM-305 is the executable
reference on the media library: a PDF a person uploads reaches the model as a file on the confidential
fallback, Word and Excel documents as the example reader's text, another person's conversation cannot
open the upload, and the source refuses a project document to an actor who may not see the project.
SPM-306 shows an agent skill that reads a project's documents through a tool result.

For reading tools, assert on both providers that a type the profile does not read reaches the model as
text from the application's reader behind the marker, that an MCP reader reads what no reader of the
application may read and receives the base64 content, that MCP readers are asked by priority, then by
server id and tool name, that a file above a reader's classification and a personal server without
the person's consent send nothing, that a personal OAuth reader the person has not connected shows
the connection card in the person's turn and none in a headless run, that a failing reader refuses
its file with `assistant-file-reader-failed` without a second reader, that the reader's text counts
against `MaxFileTokensPerTurn`, and that audit and logs hold the reader id, file id and hash, never
the content or the text. Prove a migration that moves data, such as `McpReaders`, on both providers
from the earlier schema up and back down.

For retrieved context, assert that the sample's assistant reads the project descriptions of the
person's active division that match the question, after the situation, never those of another
division, and that audit and logs carry its hash but not its content (SPM-291).

For compositions and scripts, register a small marked test catalog and assert on SQL Server and
PostgreSQL that neither feature is offered by default, that configuration and the application's
`INhAssistantCompositionSwitch` switch them on only for an agent whose code allows them, that the
switch is asked once per feature and turn with the right channel, tenant, agent and person and that a
change applies from the next turn, that an approved call of a marked tool after the switch went off is
refused with `assistant-composition-off`, that `GET admin/agents/{id}/compositions` names every reason
and answers only administrators, and that an agent created in the administration saves `scripts` only
within `UseCompositionsAsData`, exports and imports it in a package and is offered the tool only when
the ceiling, its setting and the switch all allow it (SPM-371).
